_doc: The squad brain (src/battle/land/drill.ts; Brian, 20 Nov 20:43Z: 'super realistic and meaningful and everyone has high AI iq'): what each man, tank and gun inside a block does, second by second. Looks only (ruling 217: the card decides, the field acts it out): the fight never reads any of it, so no number here can move a result.

style: the drill's numbers by the computer general's style (styles.ts), and 'plain' for a side the player commands or a battle with no styles. rush and halt: seconds a team runs forward and lies firing in fire and movement (one team rushes while the other covers it); wave: both teams go together (a mass); assault: the share of a block's riflemen who work forward onto the enemy while the rest keep its head down; spacing: metres between men in a line; tankRush, tankHalt: seconds a pair of tanks drives on while the other pair halts and covers it; scoot: the chance a tank that fired from the open backs off to cover; salvo: 'battery' (the guns fire together), 'rapid' (each as fast as it can), 'ripple' (one after another down the line); gunEvery: seconds between a gun's shots.

xp: how experience changes the men: under raw they bunch (spacing times bunch), look only a short way for cover (seek), and stay down longer when hit (pinned); from veteran they spread wide and look further.

cover: how much shelter a man finds on each ground, 0 none to 1 the best (works and bunkers); 'edge' is added where the ground in front of him toward the enemy is open (he lines the wood's or the houses' edge, never the middle), 'crest' where a fold of ground 1 to 4 m higher lies 15 m in front of him, 'wreck' and 'crater' for a man close behind a burnt-out tank or in a shell hole.

ranges (metres between blocks' edges): column, a block on the march further than this from any enemy goes in files on its road; bound, nearer than this, or under fire, it goes by fire and movement; debus, lorried infantry get down; fo, guns firing further than this have a spotter up with the foot nearest their target; ambush, a defence's anti-tank team goes to its flank once enemy tanks come within this; grenade, men this close to the enemy's men throw.
pin: a block losing this share of its strength a second (smoothed), or shelled within 'shelled' seconds, goes to ground: men in the open crawl to cover, about a third keep their heads down.

rounds._about: Every round fired (Brian, 21 November 04:04Z: 'make the right odds if they actually hit so it not always an automatic hit ... when they do hit ... it shows up on the receiving object'). Looks only (ruling 217), the drill's own dice: a man falls and a tank is knocked out only where the rules take the model, and that round is a hit. odds: [best chance, metres at which it halves] for an aimed round from a halted shooter at a halted target in the open (tank: a 75 mm class gun at a tank; at: a launcher or anti-tank rifle; gun: a field or anti-tank gun over open sights; mg and rifle: at a lorry or a gun's shield, never at a man, as a man hit is a man the rules take). Times the shooter moving, the target moving, the target's cover (crest: hull-down) and the crew's experience [at none, more at full]. glance: the share of hits on a tank that bounce, by the face struck (the rest go in and do harm short of a kill). turret: the share of hits on a tank's turret. spread: a miss's error in metres [along the line of fire, more per metre of range, across, more per metre]. indirect: a gun firing over a crest lands round its aim [metres, more per metre of range], a mortar always so (mortar: its own spread), a hit where it lands within onVehicle of a vehicle. mortar (release 2: a support team's tube) is always indirect, so its odds and spread are never read. speed: metres a second a round flies. smallArms: seconds between a rifleman's shots and a machine gun's bursts [least, most]. keep: seconds the drill keeps a round in its list; marks: the most scars one vehicle keeps.

teams._about: Support teams (release 2; Brian, 21 November 2026, 03:49Z: 'units you can place at the begining of a battle on your side and they can then attack from the back'): a machine-gun team's three guns on their tripods (role hmg) or a mortar team's three tubes (role mortar), each with its crew, carried by hand. hmg.burst: seconds between a tripod gun's bursts [least, most] (longer and closer than a section's light gun). mortar.every: a tube's shots as a share of the style's gunEvery (a mortar fires faster than a field gun). file: metres between the crews carrying their weapons in file on the march; pace: metres a battle second a crew runs its weapon to a new place in the line; sep: metres kept between two weapons set up.

sections._about: Each model drawn as its section (release 2; the 3D ground battle scene for Brian, 21 November 2026, 18:29Z: 'the ground battle needs a lot more soldiers in it'). Looks only (ruling 217): the model stays the rules' one, its key man; the rest of his section stand round him and fall one by one as the block loses strength, the last of them when the rules lift the model. rifle: a rifle section by army (the default for the rest): men in all, its leader the key man, one automatic weapon (US the BAR, Germany the MG 42, Britain the Bren), its number twos and ammunition bearers (loaders), and its scouts out ahead on the move. officer: the headquarters (the officer and his runners); mg: a machine-gun section (the gun, two loaders, its leader); at: an anti-tank team (the launcher and its loader); sapper: an assault pioneer section; holder: a horse holder and the two with him; gun: a field gun's crew (beside the gun); hmg and mortar: a support team's ammunition bearers (beside the three the 3D game draws with each weapon). Each number counts the key man: a gun's counts the gun itself (8: the gun and seven crew), hmg's and mortar's the three drawn with the weapon (7: four bearers; 8: five). space: metres between the men of a section in its line; rows: metres between a block's front and second row of sections; files: men to a file on the march (more files for more men); ahead: metres a section's scouts go before it.

platoon._about: Drawn as platoons (Brian, 22 November 2026: 'I want a lot of troops in the ground battles'): each rifle model drawn as its rifle platoon, by army. squads: its squads, the key man's own leading and the rest one behind another, step metres apart, each on its own leader and the same as the key man's section; hq: its headquarters, its leader counted, inside the leading squad's wedge. The US 3 squads of 12 and 5 (41 men), Germany 3 of 10 and a Zugtrupp of 7 (37), Britain 3 of 10 and 7 (37), the Soviets 4 of 10 and 3, Japan 3 of 13 and 4, Italy 3 of 10 and 4, France 3 of 12 and 4; the rest 3 and 4. rows: metres between a block's front and second row of platoons. Gun crews, support teams, anti-tank teams, sappers, an officer's party and tanks stay as they are.

tanks._about: A tank halted in a fight fights from alternate posts (every army but a mass, whose scoot is 0): 'shots' [least, most] from one post, then she backs 'back' metres out of sight, crosses behind the line and comes up at her next post, 'post' metres to one side of her own place and then the other (her own place is where the rules lay her wreck, so she never goes far from it).

_about: The drill book (release 2; Brian, 22 November 2026, 00:23Z: 'i want the troop AI to be smart and move like a platoon with covering fire and historical tactics ... with combines arms'): how each army's platoons fight, in src/battle/land/tactics.ts; the principles, the schools and the historian's and the general's reviews in /mnt/project-files/battles/drill-book/. Looks only (ruling 217). On when the men are drawn as platoons. Times are battle seconds (the 3D plays the fight at half the battle's clock, so a 2 s rush shows as 4 s).

schools: each army's own manual and kit. bound: who rushes with whom in the three turns of fire and movement (tactics.ts Bound: 'body' the platoon's squads a turn each, each squad as one body round its gun, the gun at its head, as a German squad; 'squad' the squads a turn each, the automatic rifle walking with its squad; 'both' the sections a turn each, each gun group a turn after its riflemen; 'wave' all together); raw and veteran: the bound at that experience where it differs. crawl: the share of rushes made at a crouched creep (infiltration), the pace allowing. final: how the assault goes in at the last ('grenade' grenades from cover then in, 'marching' walking forward firing, 'charge' the rush in with a shout from 30 to 50 m). gunStays: the assault leaves its squads' guns firing with the base of fire. counter: battle seconds after the enemy reaches a defence's line before its rear platoons counter-attack (negative: never). hold: metres to which a defence holds its fire, where its drill sets it (a Japanese defence: to 25 to 50 m).

nations: each nation's school (the historian's map, 22 November: ROM and SVK French-model armies; ESP, ARG, CHL and TUR German-trained; NOR, NED, MEX and THA by the principles); any nation not named fights by '_' (the principles as written), so every playable nation fights by the book.

rush: seconds a man is up in a rush [raw, regular, veteran] (the general: up 3 to 5 s, 10 to 20 m); gap: seconds between one turn's rush and the next's; stagger: the most seconds a pair rises after the first of its turn (by twos and threes; the leaders first). aside: after a rush, the share of men who crawl [least, most] metres aside before they fire (the enemy is aiming where they dropped).

suppress: a round landing near a group of men (a squad, a section, a crew) adds to its suppression [metres it reaches, how much it adds] by weapon; it halves every 'half' seconds [raw, regular, veteran]; above 'down' the group's men keep their heads down and its rushes wait, but for its gunner and a share 'keep' who go on firing; above 'heavy' those in the open crawl for cover. rapid: the time between shots of men covering their mates' rushes, as a share of their usual (rapid fire).

lift: metres from friendly foot within which the guns' and the mortars' rounds lift off a target into its depth ('deep' metres beyond its far side), and the support teams' machine guns shift to its far half. mission: a battery's or a mortar team's shoot at a new target, its spotter's signaller calling it on his radio: the call [least, most] seconds, one ranging round over the target ('range' metres off), a call, a second short of it, a call, then fire for effect, 'salvos' [least, most] every 'every' [least, most] seconds, then quiet [least, most] seconds and again (a call of 'again' seconds, no ranging); a mortar team's calls and quiet as a share 'mortar'. Fire over open sights is no mission.

tank: battle seconds between a tank's own aimed rounds in a fight [least, most] (the general: a round every 15 to 30 s at a weapon). tankMg (Brian, 22 November 04:10Z: 'make sure the machine gun from the gunner inside the tank also shoots some times at infantry', and 'the top machine gun cant be used unless the tank commander mans the gun'): of the men a tank block takes off the enemy's foot, the share that fall to her machine guns rather than her main gun's shells, in the open and in cover (woods, streets, works: there high explosive does more of it); each machine-gun round names its gun (g): the commander's 'roof' gun (only in the armies named, only with him up in the hatch, 'roofShare' of his tank's bursts), the hull gunner's when the target is within 'hullArc' degrees of her bow, else the 'coax' beside the main gun. A commander up in his hatch is exposed: a small-arms round that strikes his tank strikes him 'commander' of the time, a shell bursting on her 'splinter' of the time (the round carries cm: 1); she fights buttoned up from then, and her roof gun is silent. hold: metres to which a defence holds its fire: its machine guns, its riflemen [raw, regular, veteran] (the general: machine guns 300 to 400 m, rifles 200, veterans 100, raw troops open at 600 to 800 and give themselves away). counter: a defence counter-attacks once the enemy is within 'at' metres of its line, its rear platoons going 'ahead' metres forward of their places; xp: its pause times this [raw, regular, veteran]. flank: metres [least, most] the assault's men swing out toward the flank on a rush ('rush'), and the most they swing out from their places in the line ('out': the general, inside a platoon 40 to 60 m). smoke: as an assault goes out its platoons lay the school's 'smoke' rounds (a British platoon's 2-inch mortar 3; none for the Soviets) side by side 'spread' metres apart on the enemy's front corner on its flank, again every 'every' seconds while it is out; no harm (the 3D draws a screen drifting with the battle's wind); off ('on' false) until the 3D scene draws smoke rounds. With smoke on call (the battle's smoke switch, release 2, ruling 242 S6) the platoons lay none of these: each screen the rules lay (LandBattle.screens) is drawn as rounds from the block's base of fire, one each 'per' metres of its line, at most 'most' (the design director's looks-only knobs), each hanging ('hang') till the screen's end.

Squad life (release 2; Brian, 25 November 2026, 13:40Z: 'i dont want all the soldiers of a squad doing the exact same thing at the same time. I want them to work together and look real as individuals apart of a squad'). Looks only (ruling 217), the drill's own dice; on only where asked (Drill life: the 3D game's 'Squads of individuals' switch), and the drill book is on with it. A squad still does one thing together (it rushes in its turn, holds its line, falls back), but each man does his own part of it in his own time.

Buddy teams: a squad's men pair off (its leader and his runner, its gun with its number twos, its riflemen two by two along each arm of its wedge). rush: in fire and movement a squad's teams rise one after another over 'spread' turns of the cycle (each cycle in a fresh order), not all in the same second, so some of a squad are always down firing while its others run; a wave's teams rise within 'wave' seconds; each man's own rush lasts 'len' [least, most] of his army's; the fast (rolling) advance drops its teams to fire one at a time over 'roll' seconds, a share 'knee' of the men only to a knee. A man left more than about 'sprint' metres behind his place sprints upright till he has made it up, and at any time a share 'upright' of the men run head up where the rest go bent low, each for a spell of his own.

drift: on the move no line is dressed as on parade: each man drifts up to 'along' metres ahead of and behind his place and 'across' to either side of it, over 'every' [least, most] seconds of his own. rout: in a rout the share in headlong flight, and the share running upright with their rifles (the rest bent low), each for a spell of his own.

react: seconds [least, most] over which a squad's men take up a new order, never all in one moment. rise: a man lying or kneeling who must get up and go (his block gone on, its line swung round) gets up within this many seconds, his own moment; leash: each man's own slack, up to this many metres, before a block going on without him gets him up; calm: a change of the squad's task within this many seconds of its last is taken up by all at once (a squad creeping forward in a firefight changes from moving to firing and back each half second: no man's moment is set back by that). ground: going to ground when fire comes (raw men 'raw' times slower); up: getting up to move, the leader's team first and the rest by teams; settle: taking their firing places as the squad halts; back: falling back, the gun team last; break: a rout (a few go, then the rest); rally: gathering again.

watch: holding or waiting, the men of a squad take different stances by what shelters each (open: the share lying; cover: woods, a bank, a wreck; works: fieldworks and houses) and each keeps his for 'keep' [least, most] seconds of his own; 'sentries' of each squad kneel watching, the duty passing on every 'turn' [least, most] seconds; far from the enemy ('far' metres) a share 'easy' stand easy; its leader has his glasses up a share 'glasses' of the time.

scan: a man watching faces his own way: his own lean of up to 'own' radians off the squad's front, a fresh look every 'every' [least, most] seconds within 'arc' radians (sentries the whole of it, the rest 'rest' of it, a man lying 'lying' of it), turning his head and shoulders at 'rate' radians a second; a leader looks along his line to his men a share 'back' of his looks.

pause: a man firing from the line breaks off every 'every' [least, most] seconds for 'for' [least, most] (a fresh clip, a look for his target); a machine gun every 'gun' [least, most] seconds for 'gunFor' (a new belt or drum, a hot barrel).

ready: on the approach, not yet under fire, the distance from the enemy at which each man brings his rifle to the ready, as a share of rifle range (ranges.bound), by his own number between 'ready' [least, most]: the scouts and the wary first, the rest trotting on with rifles at the port.

tankmg._about: A tank's machine guns, seen firing (release 2; Brian, 25 November 2026, 15:55Z: 'i never see the machine guns on the tanks firing'; 15:56Z: 'i dont want it to be all the time as thats unrealistic with ammo'). Looks only (ruling 217), the drill's own dice; on only where asked (Drill tankmg: the 3D game's switch).

exits._about: Men who leave the field are seen leaving (release 2; Brian, 25 November 2026, 17:11Z: 'some soldiers freeze and then disapear'). Looks only (ruling 217), the drill's own dice; on only where asked (Drill exits: the 3D game's switch). The men of a routing block run on past the field's edge. The men of a block that has left the fight (fled off the field, or withdrawn at its out line) stay drawn, each going for his own edge: a withdrawn block's man gets up and turns in his own moment, 0 to 'rise' battle seconds after it left, and runs at his own 'pace' [least, most] metres a battle second; vehicles drive at their block's pace. Each is dropped from the list once 'past' metres beyond his edge, or 'cap' battle seconds after his block left.

wounded._about: Wounded and knocked-down men (release 2; Brian, 25 November 2026, 16:14Z: 'im not seeing multiple soliders being taken out by an explosion if they are in the blast radius'). Looks only (ruling 217), the drill's own dice; the rules' losses stay as booked; on only where asked (Drill wounded: the 3D game's switch).

paces._about: Every man his own pace (release 2; Brian, 25 November 2026, 17:30Z: 'it looks like they are all jogging at the same speed'; 16:24Z: 'the soldiers of a squad keep zig zaging at the same time'). Looks only (ruling 217), the drill's own dice; the rules never read it; on only where asked (Drill paces: the 3D game's switch, off until a Mac off/on line and the art director pass it). The numbers are laid here by the build.

hatch._about: Heads up, hatches down (release 2; Brian, 25 November 2026, 15:11Z: 'do those 3 ideas'). Looks only (ruling 217), the drill's own dice; on only where asked (Drill hatches: the 3D game's switch). A tank's commander rides with his head out of his hatch, for the view, until something sends him down: a round at his own tank, a shell bursting within 'burst' metres of her, or the enemy within his own nerve of it: 'near' metres by his crew's experience [raw, regular, veteran], each commander his own share 'own' [least, most] of it. He drops inside 'drop' seconds [least, most] after the first of it (times 'quick' by experience: a veteran is down at once) and comes up again once nothing has troubled him for 'quiet' seconds by experience (his own share 'own' of it): a green commander closes up early and stays down long, a veteran rides heads up until the rounds are at him and is up again soon after. A round at another tank of his block sends him down too a share 'mates' of the time, by experience. A commander struck in his hatch (book.tankMg) stays down. Off, a block's tanks close up as one with the enemy inside 120 m.

seasoned._about: Experience you can see (release 2; Brian, 25 November 2026, 15:11Z: 'do those 3 ideas'). Looks only (ruling 217), the drill's own dice; on only where asked and only with squad life (Drill seasoned: the 3D game's switch).

leaders._about: When the leader falls (release 2; Brian, 25 November 2026, 15:11Z: 'do those 3 ideas'). Looks only (ruling 217), the drill's own dice; on only where asked and only with squad life (Drill leaders: the 3D game's switch).

_about: Tanks with minds of their own (release 2; Brian, 25 November 2026, 15:57Z: 'i dont want the tanks and vehicles doing the exact same thing as each other. i want everything to see like it has its own mind'). Looks only (ruling 217), the drill's own dice; on only where asked (Drill tankmind: the 3D game's switch).

Timing and movement (Brian, 15:56Z: 'should the tanks be moving or was that the real tactic?': the real drill was move, halt briefly to fire, move on, one of a pair covering while the other moves). Times are battle seconds (the 3D game plays the fight at half the battle's clock, so a 2 s halt shows as 4 s). The block's place and pace stay the rules': a tank only falls behind her place and catches up.

react: seconds [least, most] each tank's commander takes to take up his block's new phase, his own each time; the platoon leader (its first tank) at once; till then she goes on with what she was at (and, told to stand and wait for her place to come up to her on the fast advance, she rolls on slowly that long: no platoon stops in one instant). quick: times this by her crew's training [raw, regular, veteran] (the block's experience, never its nation). The same wait, by her own dice, before she turns about when her block's way turns about under her (the rules jostle it back in a fight): a jostle shorter than it never turns her. roll: metres a battle second at which a tank counts her block as rolling on fast: she leaves the fast drill below the first, and takes it up at the second (two numbers, so a block near the pace does not send her to and fro). straight: the pace is the block's own where its way over the last three seconds was at least this straight (the ground it made over the way it went); less straight than that (the rules jostle a block to and fro in a fight), it counts for that much less, so a block shoved about that gains little ground is coming on slowly and its tanks leapfrog. way: coming on with a block that goes that straight, a tank's way is the way the block has made over those three seconds, where it makes this many metres a second or more that way, not the way of its last step (the rules shove a block a little aside from step to step: she is not swung from side to side with it). back: coming on, a tank backs no further than this many metres toward the enemy, her rear to him, nor with no enemy about: her nose turned away from her way (a block shoved about turns its tanks round), she turns about where she stands and drives on, where the plain drill would have her back along with her block for as long as it goes slowly.

halt: move, halt briefly to fire, move on, on the fast advance. reach: metres from the enemy within which she halts to fire. rare: rolling on fast she halts to fire this many times less often than she fires in a fight (her period between rounds times this), which keeps the rounds she fires on the fast advance about as many as before (a block shoved to and fro at a fast pace, its tanks leapfrogging, fires as seldom). soon: seconds before her round is due at which she presses on 'ahead' metres before her place, to buy her halt. len: seconds [least, most] she stands, her own wish each time (she takes the longest she can afford, never under the least). lay: seconds [least, most] she stands laying her gun before her round goes, on the advance and at any halt (so no round is fired in the moment she stops); see: the least seconds she stands on after it, to see it strike. fall: the most metres a halt may leave her behind her place, counting the ground her block makes while she stands and while she gathers way again (no halt she cannot afford is begun); edge: metres she keeps inside her block's leash at the end of it. apart: seconds between two halts beginning in one platoon. A tank never halts while her partner stands (pairs: first and second tank, third and fourth; a last odd tank with the pair before hers), and never more than half the platoon stands at once.
top: the fastest a tank closes up on her place after a halt, metres a battle second (the plain drill's is 12; her block's own pace where the rules drive it faster).

pair: where the block goes slowly the pairs leapfrog by the style's clock (style tankRush, tankHalt), one tank of each pair driving on to her next firing place while her partner stands covering, then the other way about, the second pair a quarter of the clock after the first. own: each tank's own lean on that clock, seconds either way, so no two move off together; len: her drive's length as a share of the style's tankRush [least, most], fresh each turn. She drives fast enough to be in her next firing place before her turn to cover comes: the way to it over her drive's seconds less 'gather' (the second she takes to gather way), never under the plain drill's pace for the bound and never over 'pace' metres a second unless that is faster. Not there when her turn to cover comes, she stands where she is (halt.edge and halt.fall as on the fast advance). And a platoon never all stands while it comes on: a tank with no mate on the move drives on, her turn to cover or not. rare: covering, she fires this many times less often than in a fight (her period between rounds times this): she now stands in every turn to cover, where the plain drill drove her on through many of them, and this keeps the rounds drawn about as many as before.

shot: her firing rhythm. first: seconds [least, most] after her block's fight begins before she may open, her own, so a platoon never fires its first volley as one; fresh: a fight counts as begun again after this many seconds out of one. pause: each pause between her rounds is her own share [least, most] of her period (the plain drill's 6 to 10 s at armour, the drill book's at foot), fresh after every round: about as many rounds as before, never evenly spaced.

keep: seconds [least, most] a tank keeps her direction, forward or backing, before she may change it again, her own (a driver does not go from forward to reverse and back each half second): she stands till then. A reverse she is ordered into (falling back, backing out of a firing post) is taken at once, and so is her block's call back inside its leash where it has left her outside.

Looking, posts, the other vehicles and the guns (step two). hull: a standing tank's hull is turned toward her block's main threat, her thickest armour to him, and her turret is free to lay on her own target or to watch her arc; 'hull' is how far to one side of him she may stand it, radians, her own at each firing post (halted to fire a moment on the fast advance she keeps her hull on her way; waiting there for her place to come up, it is turned to the threat as any standing tank's). fixed: the models whose gun is fixed in the hull (no turret): they turn their hull to fire as before, and watch no arcs with a turret; halted with nothing to lay on, each stands her hull on her own slice of watch.cone about the threat, across the line as they stand (her hull is her gun), and is sent no aim. The drill knows a model's name where the rules name it (a set piece's blocks, tank destroyers); a stand-in the 3D game alone picks for a campaign battle it cannot know.

watch: turrets watching their own arcs, when a tank has nothing to lay on. reach: metres [halted, on the move] from the enemy (the plain drill's own distances): coming on, a tank whose block is not fighting lays on him within the second and watches her arc beyond it; halted in a fight's place or pinned, she lays on him within the first though her block is not fighting just then. Halted and not fighting (holding, resting, on the start line): the platoon covers all round between its tanks, the last tank of three or more the rear half and the others an equal share each of the front half (two tanks or one share all round), across the line as they stand; with the enemy within the first reach the front shares close to 'cone' radians about him, each still her own slice. Each looks at one bearing of her share for 'hold' seconds [least, most], her own each time, then at another, and takes up her watch only her own share of 'first' seconds after she has nothing to lay on (so a platoon's guns never swing off together). far: metres out the point she looks at is sent (the 3D game lays the turret on a point). On the march in column and on the approach: alternate tanks watch left and right, between 'side' radians [least, most] off her way, and the last tank of three or more the rear, within 'rear' radians of dead astern. Where nothing is to be watched (routing, backing off with no enemy about) the gun comes back dead ahead: a point ahead is sent, since the 3D game holds the last aim it was given.

post: hull down in defence, any style. A tank halted with her block (holding, in a fight) whose firing place has cover of one of the kinds in 'cover' to sit behind sits back from it: 'down' metres straight back, at 'pace' metres a second, comes up to fire and backs down again, each at her own moment. Not fighting and the enemy far, she backs down her own share of 'idle' seconds [least, most] after she came to stand; the enemy come within watch.reach she comes up her own share of 'rise' seconds later. In a fight she backs down 'see' seconds [least, most] after her round, her own each time, where the wait for her next is long enough for the trip down and up, and comes up in time to lay and fire it at her own moment (the rounds she fires stay as many); her block's fight begun with her down, she comes up her own moment (react, quick) after it began. open: her chance each round to back down so from a place with no such cover (0, never: there is nothing there to sit behind, and the to and fro in the open reads as the flick this build calms; above 0 she backs off and comes up again in the open too). near: a shell landing within this many metres of her is a near miss; jump: her chance to take one as her cue to shift to her next post (a hit on her always is); rest: seconds [least, most] she must have been at a post before a near miss or a hit moves her, her own at each post. The shift itself is the plain drill's (back out of sight, across behind the line, up at the next post), now open to every style when its block defends or is halted in a fight; a style with no posts of its own (scoot 0) shifts only on these cues.

out: armoured cars, AA vehicles, jeeps and motorcycles (the vehicle-only squads). spot: each keeps her own place, up to these metres [across, along] off the plain drill's. start: metres [least, most] her place must have moved off from her before she drives after it, her own (the plain drill's is 5 for all), and she moves off her own moment (react, quick) after that, as she does when her place leaps (the screen called in or sent out); pace: her own share [least, most] of the plain drill's pace when closing up; trail: while her block drives she keeps up to this many seconds of its pace further back, her own share, and closes up when it halts, so each stops at her own moment; far: beyond this many metres from her place she drives straight for it, nearer she keeps pace with it. sight: a car's turret lays on her own point of the enemy block within this many metres (the plain drill's distance; one point for all before); further off she watches her own flank, between 'arc' radians [least, most] off her block's front, as a tank watches (watch.hold, watch.far). An AA vehicle's gun, standing, watches her own share of all round, and on the move comes back dead ahead. Jeeps and motorcycles are given no aim, as before. Standing, each turns her nose toward the threat her own way (up to twice 'hull').

lean: lorries, the armoured infantry's carriers, a battery's tractors and its guns on the move (self-propelled, or each behind her own tractor) keep each her own place, up to these metres [across, along] off the plain drill's, and each moves off from standing at her own moment (react, quick), never all in one instant; the first of a column at once. The third number: in column each keeps this many seconds of the block's pace further behind the one ahead (and up to as much again, her own share), so the column strings out at speed and closes up at the halt, each rolling on to her place and stopping at her own moment. The men aboard ride as before. volley: a battery's guns fire as a ripple whatever its style: each gun her own moment within 'own' seconds of the order, never within 'apart' seconds of another gun of her battery (the ranging gun of the drill book's mission fires alone as before).

wait: on the fast advance a tank well ahead of her place (her block keeps its tanks behind its own foot on close ground, or has checked) waits for it to come up to her; the platoon does not all stand while it waits. Its pairs take turns to roll on slowly, one tank of each pair at a time: 'turn' seconds for a pair's whole turn (half each), 'own' seconds of her own lean on it, so no two move off together; 'pace' metres a battle second, and never more than half her block's pace, so her place still comes up to her; and never more than 'far' metres further ahead of her place than where the plain drill has her stop to wait, nor out of her block's leash; and only while her block goes steadily on (one the rules shove to and fro may leap off another way, and she waits standing, as before). weave: rolling on with her block, a tank does not hold her hull dead parallel to her mates': she steers a little to one side of her way and back again, up to her own 'side' radians [least, most] off it (the point she steers for moved across her way by that share of its distance from her), once every her own 'len' seconds [least, most]. back (above) also counts the ground she has already backed: coming on, once she has backed that many metres toward the enemy she turns about, however near the place she backs to.

blast._about: Shell blasts (release 2; Brian, 23 November 05:04Z: 'explosions on the ground should be able to take out multiple people if they are close to it'). Looks only, the rules' counts untouched (Drill.thin): with LandBattle.blast on, the men a block loses to a gun's or a tank's high explosive wait up to 'hold' battle seconds for one burst, or until as many are due as one shell of the class takes ('most', a realistic few: men of a section stand 5 to 10 m apart); a 'shell' event that took a key man within 'anchor' seconds is that burst. The men nearest it fall, within shells.ts REACH of it; a man lying down counts his distance over 'lying', kneeling over 'kneeling' (a burst finds him less: fragments fly up and out).

escort._about: Infantry with tanks (release 2; Brian, 23 November 05:05Z: 'have them advance behind the tank using it as cover like they would in real life ... make sure their players cant be run over by their own vechiles and they get out of the way. vechiles can run over enemy soldiers though which would kill them'). Looks only (LandBattle.escort, Drill.escort and clearOfVehicles): a foot block deploying or bounding forward with a friendly tank within 'near' metres sends up to 'men' riflemen within 'reach' of her to file in behind her, 'gap' metres back, 'file' apart, 'side' either side of her tracks, at her pace plus a little ('pace' its least and most, m/s); a tank or lorry is moving over 'moving' m/s. 'clear': a man of her side within 'ahead' metres of her nose (or 'behind' of her middle) and 'half' of her middle line steps out to 'out' metres of it at a run, not again for 'dodge' seconds; an enemy only once within 'enemyAhead', and never while lying pinned; a man the rules take from his block while within 'crush' ahead and 'crushHalf' aside of an enemy tank's middle on the move is run over. 'within': blocks this far beyond a vehicle are not looked at.

mech._about: Armoured infantry (release 2; Brian, 23 November 07:01Z, yes to 'half-tracks carrying armoured infantry'; LandBattle.mech, off unless turned on; looks only). An armoured block draws the riflemen of its division riding behind its tanks, a section to each carrier, who get down near the enemy as lorried infantry do. 'rows': the historian's (23 November 07:05Z, historian/halftracks-td-spg-movers-1123.md, M unless said), each army's carriers to a block of four tanks, [from, until, models] by the battle's year (a fraction for the month), drawn in that order and as many as the block's tray over four of them (one at least); an army with no row draws none. Britain's Universal Carrier is not modelled: its row draws the lorries beside it (the known list). The Soviet tank riders and the minor armies wait for their own rows. Units decide (the design director, 07:19Z): these rows are only the history start's mix; where the campaign says what a corps carries, 'kit' draws it. 'commonwealth': drawn as Britain's. 'armoured': carriers whose riders a bullet cannot reach while they are aboard (the design director, 07:06Z(2): struck through the vehicle's armour; a man aboard is not the next to fall to small arms). 'share': the riflemen's share of an armoured block's men, so a scaled battle draws as many as its men at that scale (an armoured division about 0.3, M). 'back': metres behind the block's tray their middle keeps. 'base': their k from this up (the 3D game tells a man by block, k and j).

kit._about: Units decide (the design director, 23 November 07:19Z): where the campaign says what a corps carries (ForceKit.halftracks, its share of half-tracks), the rows above set only the history start's mix. 'per': carriers to four tanks; 'models': an army's own half-track; an army with none of its own draws the stand-in in its own coat (the Axis' the Sd.Kfz. 251, the rest the M3), said on the known list.

spg._about: Self-propelled guns (release 2; Brian, 23 November 07:01Z, yes to 'a tank destroyer and a self-propelled gun for each major army'; LandBattle.spg, off unless turned on; looks only; a campaign battle's only, set pieces stay as the historian drew them). Some of a battery's guns are drawn as its army's self-propelled howitzer: no tractor, no crew on foot, firing when the battery fires and moving with it. 'rows': the historian's (23 November 07:05Z, historian/halftracks-td-spg-movers-1123.md, H): [from, until, models, per, with] by the battle's year (a fraction for the month): its side's blocks of that army of a kind in 'with' each bring 'per' of them (the US an M7 battery behind each armoured block; Britain's Priests, then Sextons, behind theirs; Germany's Hummel battery of six in a panzer division; the Soviet SU-76 regiment of each rifle division), taken from that army's batteries in the order of their blocks, a battery's first guns first (they stand longest), the models in turn. An army with no row draws none (Italy's Semovente is drawn as a tank destroyer; Japan had none worth drawing). Units decide (the design director, 23 November 07:19Z): these rows are only the history start's mix; where the campaign says what a corps has (ForceKit.spg, its share of its guns self-propelled), 'kit' draws it, its army's own model or the stand-in in its coat.

td._about: Tank destroyers (release 2, the same yes; LandBattle.td, off unless turned on; looks only; a campaign battle's only). The design director, 23 November 07:28Z, (a): a tank destroyer may be one model in an armoured block's mix, as the StuG is; the block keeps its own figures and fights as ever; a whole block of them waits for Units decide to give corps tank-destroyer battalions with figures of their own. ForceKit.td reads first (its share of the block's tanks), its army's own model ('kit') or the stand-in in its coat; else the historian's rows (23 November 07:05Z, H), [from, until, models, share] by the battle's year: the Soviet SU-85 with the tank blocks from August 1943, Italy's Semovente with the armoured blocks to its armistice. The tanks drawn so are spread through the block (a share of a quarter: its fourth tank of each four). Germany's StuG is in its stand-in mix already; the American and British M10 went with the infantry, so they come by the kit.

cars._about: Armoured cars (release 2; Brian, 23 November 07:01Z, yes to armoured cars, jeeps, motorcycles and AA; LandBattle.cars, off unless turned on; looks only; a campaign battle's only; the design director, 07:47Z, accepted as proposed). A block's cars are a view of it: out 'ahead' metres before its front, 'side' metres beyond each flank, while it has not met the enemy ('contact' metres) and is not fighting; then back 'back' metres behind its tray. They see nothing the block does not (no ticket words say they scout), fire never, and are lost as the block's strength goes. 'rows': the historian's (23 November 07:47Z, historian/armoured-cars-aa-1123.md, H for where, M for the counts): [from, until, model, {kind: per block}] by the battle's year; 'per' below one is 1 in so many of the side's blocks of that army and kind, in the order of their blocks (a half: every other one). Every row of the month counts. Units decide: ForceKit.cars (its corps' cars per block) reads first, its army's own model or the stand-in; the rows are only the history start's.

aa._about: AA vehicles (release 2, the same yes; LandBattle.aa, off unless turned on; looks only; a campaign battle's only). A block's AA vehicles are a view of it, kept 'back' metres behind its tray (a battery's behind its tractors, 'battery' more), moving with it; lost as its strength goes. They hit nothing the rules do not take, and a strike's losses stay the rules'; until the 3D game aims them upward they ride and park. 'rows': the historian's (23 November 07:47Z, historian/armoured-cars-aa-1123.md), read as the cars' are ('art': a battery, not a support team). Units decide: ForceKit.aa (its corps' AA vehicles per block) reads first.

light._about: Jeeps, field cars and motorcycles (release 2; Brian, 23 November 07:01Z, yes to armoured cars, jeeps, motorcycles and AA; LandBattle.light, off unless turned on; looks only; a campaign battle's only; as the armoured cars, the design director's 07:47Z ruling). A block's light vehicles are a view of it: those 'ahead' ride out on its flanks ('ahead' metres before its front, 'side' beyond each flank) while it has not met the enemy (the armoured cars' 'contact'), then keep behind it; those behind park at its rear corners ('back'), and a motorcycle there rides despatch, back 'run' metres and up again each 'every' seconds. They see nothing the block does not, fire never, and are lost as the block's strength goes; never more than 'most' to a block, cars first. 'cars' and 'bikes' rows: the historian's (23 November 08:18Z, historian/light-cars-motorcycles-1123.md; H for where, M for most counts): by army ('_' every army not named), [from, until, models (taken in turn), {kind: per block}, {kind: 'ahead'} (else behind)]; 'per' below one is 1 in so many of the side's blocks of that army and kind, in the order of their blocks. 'kit': each army's own model where the campaign says what the corps has (ForceKit.jeeps, ForceKit.bikes); 'stand' the rest's, in their own coat. 'sw': the swaps a model is drawn with by army ('sidecar' on for the Poles, French, Hungarians and Romanians); a car riding ahead keeps her machine gun, one behind is a staff car without it.
